items.title: Land values data, often overlooked, is now missing from economic debate
paras: Experts say it is important to have publicly available national land value data that is aggregated in an independent and credible way. ( ABC NEWS: Tanjim Islam )
Our food comes from it. Our cities are built on it. And the "value" of land is a central element in our economic system.
It is surprising, then, to learn that the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) has stopped publishing data on the value of residential, commercial, and rural land in the National Accounts.
Public policy experts use that data to inform their thinking about housing, land use, our cities, and so much more.
The ABC understands there has been substantial pushback to the ABS's decision to stop publishing the data. It has been significant enough that the ABS may end up reversing it.
Last month, the ABS mentioned on its website that it has decided to stop publishing these 14 tables in the Australian System of National Accounts:
The ABS made the decision for resourcing and budgetary reasons. It looked at its website analytics to see what data people were downloading and made the decision from there.
It says the data will no longer be published but estimates may be made available on request to the ABS.

As the economy evolves over time, some datasets can become less useful for analysts or much harder to collect, and the ABS has to keep an eye on its resourcing and decide which datasets to keep publishing.
In the past it has consulted with the public before cancelling datasets, but this time it decided to cancel the datasets and see what response it got from the public.
In this case, some complaints have come in from economists, public policy experts, and think tanks about the land value data specifically.

They have said it is important to have publicly available national data that is aggregated in an independent and credible way. Since governments are actively making policy changes that directly impact land values, it would be very unhelpful if the data stopped being published.
But if their protests are successful, any reversal by the ABS may not happen until next year.

So while we wait, it is interesting to think about how land and "land values" can often be an afterthought, or neglected, in some economic pedagogy and why missing data on national land values could feed into that.

For example, when studying economics you might be told about a French economist called Léon Walras (1834-1910) who helped to formulate the marginal theory of value and pioneer general equilibrium theory.
Walras was one of the founding fathers of the "marginalist revolution" and neoclassical economics.

But Walras was also deeply concerned about social justice; he was vehemently anti-monopoly and believed that land and natural resources had to be held in public hands for the competitive market system to work properly.

But he said the state should lease land and natural resources to entrepreneurs in agriculture, industry and commerce. That way, the state would capture the rising rents of land that belonged to the community and it could use that revenue to support the nation, while abolishing income taxes.
Why are Walras's views about the centrality of land in our social and economic system often forgotten, while his work on the price adjustment process in markets is not?
His views were very similar to another economist called Henry George . In fact, the American economist Milton Friedman tells a funny story about "Georgites" after visiting Australia in 1981.
Milton Friedman said he kept bumping into fans of Henry George in Australia. ( Wikimedia Commons )
Friedman noted in his memoir that wherever he spoke in Australia there always seemed to be someone in the audience who wanted to talk about Henry George and land taxation.

"One notable feature of the many public sessions we participated in was the almost invariable question from the floor from a Henry Georgite persuaded that land-value taxation was the panacea for all of Australia's difficulties," he wrote.

"Over the years, I have had many contacts with Georgites, who are on the whole very sensible, except for overestimating the uniqueness of land, underestimating the difficulty of distinguishing the 'original and indestructible' qualities of the soil from those imparted by investment, and overestimating the revenues and favourable effects from their pet single tax.
"I have generally compromised with Georgites by agreeing that a pure land tax is one of the least bad taxes that is possible," he wrote.
Those little stories are a roundabout way of saying that publicly available national data on land values is quite important.
The question of land, and who is capturing the rising "value" of land from the wider community's economic activity over time, has a huge amount of public interest value.

The topic of land ownership and its links with economic activity, income, and the distribution of wealth, is of perpetual interest in certain circles and is scattered through the history of economic thought.
The German economist Isabella Weber, in her recent best-selling book Anti-Fascist Economics , also makes the link between land and life's essentials.

She said Walras's belief that land had to be in public hands for markets to work fairly suggested that any outcome from trading in the marketplace was heavily dependent on the prior distribution of resources before trading occurred.

"This is the opposite conclusion to the standard approach in economics that insists we need to rely on market distribution in the first place and then redistribute — and the redistribution too often remains an afterthought," she wrote.

Last week, the Financial Times chief economics commentator Martin Wolf selected Weber's book as one of the best books of 2026 in economics. The themes in her book are big, and the value of land is linked to many of them.
So, let us see if the ABS ends up reversing its decision to stop publishing land value data in the National Accounts.
It is the type of data that contributes to some of the biggest arguments in economics.

items.title: ASX set to slip as Wall Street falls; Anthropic tumbles below IPO price, Nvidia slumps
paras: Advertisement Business Markets World markets ASX set to slip as Wall Street falls; Anthropic tumbles below IPO price, Nvidia slumps Stan Choe November 25, 2026 — 5:26am
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Share A A A Stocks tied to the artificial intelligence industry are dragging the US market lower after their surge from the day before quickly fizzled. That’s even though much of the rest of Wall Street is rising, along with confidence among Americans in the economy.

The S&P 500 fell 0.3 per cent and is heading toward its eighth loss in the last nine days. Tech stocks once again led the way lower and dragged the Nasdaq composite down a market-leading 1.3 per cent, in early afternoon trade. Stocks outside of AI held up much better, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 441 points, or 0.9 per cent.

AI stocks weighed down Wall Street on Tuesday after Monday’s Nvidia-driven surge. Bloomberg The Australian sharemarket is set to slip, with futures at 5.04am AEDT pointing to a loss 0f 6 points, or 0.1 per cent, at the open. The ASX added 1.8 per cent on Tuesday. The Australian dollar was stronger at US66.44¢.

They’re the latest swings for a market that’s been mostly sinking since setting its all-time high last month. The primary worry is that prices for AI-related stocks shot too high into a possible bubble and need to deflate. That carries immense consequences for the broader market and workers’ retirement accounts because AI companies have grown into Wall Street’s most influential stocks.

While the surprise return of Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s CEO announced does bring back a charismatic leader who championed and helped build the entire AI industry, it does not settle the deep concerns dogging it. For one, doubts remain about whether AI can possibly produce enough profit and productivity to make the massive investments underway in data centres worth it.

At the same time, high interest rates make it more difficult to borrow money to pay for the industry’s growth. Sweeping victories for Democrats earlier this month in the US midterm elections, meanwhile, have raised concerns about more regulation for AI, including possible halts to further construction of data centres.
To be sure, AI stocks and the broader US market have been prone to extreme reversals since the summer, not only week to week but even hour to hour.
Nvidia fell 7.1 per cent a day after soaring 31.5 per cent to its biggest gain in more than two decades. Other stocks around the AI industry fell by similar amounts.
CoreWeave, which buys Nvidia chips and rents out access to them over the cloud, sank 11.6 per cent. GE Vernova, which is helping to power AI data centres, dropped 4.6 per cent.

And Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, tumbled 7.4 per cent to drop below $US83. That’s how much Anthropic first sold its stock for in its initial public offering last week. The stock had briefly jumped as high as $US115 in its first day of trading amid a frenzy of hype.

Such drops were powerful enough to drag the S&P 500 index lower even though the majority of stocks within the index climbed. They rose following the latest report to say confidence among US consumers is improving by more than economists expected.

Confidence jumped sharply for Democrats and independents following the midterm election results, according to the Conference Board. That narrowed the wide gap between them and Republicans, whose confidence fell slightly. The results echo a preliminary report from the University of Michigan released earlier in the month, which also showed a jump in sentiment following the midterm elections and a drop in oil prices from late October.
Companies in industries across the economy, meanwhile, continue to report strong growth in profits for the summer.

Dollar Tree climbed 12.5 per cent after reporting better earnings for the latest quarter than analysts expected. The average shopper spent slightly more in its stores during the three months than a year earlier, and more of them came in than last year.

Kohl’s rallied 18.9 per cent after reporting a profit for the latest quarter, when analysts were expecting basically zero. It also gave forecasts for revenue for the final three months of its fiscal year that were better than expected.

Businesses in the S&P 500 are on pace to report overall growth in earnings per share of more than 25 per cent for a third straight quarter, according to FactSet. That’s a big deal because stock prices tend to follow the path of corporate profits and interest rates over the long term. But emotions of investors can also overwhelm them in the short term, as the last few weeks have demonstrated.
In the bond market, Treasury yields slipped as investors moved into investments seen as safer bets. The yield on the 10-year Treasury fell to 4.91 per cent from 4.92 per cent late on Monday.

That was despite a rise in oil prices, which tend to push upward on inflation and on bond yields. The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil rose 1.7 per cent to $US88.14. It’s been yo-yoing between $US72 and $US114 since the United States and Israel attacked Iran in February.

In stock markets abroad, indexes were mixed across Europe and Asia. South Korea’s Kospi jumped 6.3 per cent, and Japan’s Nikkei 225 rallied 3.9 per cent for two of the world’s bigger moves, as they caught up to Monday’s surge from Wall Street.

items.title: Hobart stadium cost political debate still rages, despite its future being assured
paras: Both the Liberal government and Labor Opposition support the Hobart stadium project. ( Supplied: Cox Architecture )
The Braddon Labor MP and social media phenom posted his initial reaction to the Macquarie Point stadium's new estimated cost of $1.23 billion.
The cost rises to $1.54 billion if you include the project costs and precinct infrastructure — most of which was included in the previous $1.13 billion estimate.
Labor MP, Shane Broad, says its unlikely debate over the stadium will end. ( ABC News: Maren Preuss )
You wouldn't have guessed it from question time, where the Labor opposition asked zero questions about the project — but he was correct, the debate is not over.

A December 2025 promise by Premier Jeremy Rockliff, made to Independent MLC Bec Thomas to secure her vote for the stadium, to cap the state's contribution at $875 million will be broken unless the money comes in from somewhere else.
This comes after breaking a 2024 state election promise of spending $375 million "and not a red cent more".
It now seems the state will be contributing upwards of $1.25 billion — the difference funded through borrowings, Mr Rockliff has admitted.
Another broken promise is a political hit which the premier has no choice but to wear.
His admission that commitments are only commitments at a certain "point in time" was revealing.
A commitment you might choose to break later isn't really a commitment.

Of course, the state's greyhound racing community has already formed a view on the value of a promise from Jeremy Rockliff , after he announced plans to wind up the industry just weeks after guaranteeing his support for it.
The premier has said the stadium won't be headed back to parliament for another vote — in his view, its ticking off last year is enough.
But he's set to face increasing scrutiny as the lower house continues the final parliamentary sitting week of the year.
Ms Thomas is yet to speak, but said last week that if the cost cap of $875 million couldn't be kept, then the project shouldn't go ahead.
Kristie Johnson has long opposed the stadium build. ( ABC News: Owain Stia James )
Today, a bill from Independent MP Kristie Johnston is set for debate — if passed, the government would be required to seek parliament's approval to break the cost cap.

Yesterday, motions calling for the cost cap to be abided by, and another calling for more information on what's included in the new cost estimate both failed, after Labor sided with the government to block them.
It's no coincidence the loudest voices on this broken commitment have also been opposed to the project.
Had it come in just under budget, there's little chance the Greens would have suddenly jumped on board.
As worthy as this spend may be in the eyes of some, Tasmania's budget hardly has hundreds of millions spare to spend .
But there's not much anyone can do while Labor is backing in the project.
A render of the proposed Macquarie Point stadium in Hobart. ( Supplied: Macquarie Point Development Corporation )
The opposition hasn't escaped unharmed, despite its attempt to dodge the conversation in question time yesterday.
Upon revealing that Labor would not back a Greens motion calling for the cost cap to be reinstated, Josh Willie momentarily became a bigger target than the government.
"He is a disgrace," said independent MP Kristie Johnston, once again referring to the crossbench as the "true opposition".
Rosalie Woodruff says parliament could exercise its right to make the government bring it back for approval if Labor came on board. ( ABC News: Owain Stia James )
Green Leader Rosalie Woodruff accused Labor of giving the government a "blank cheque".
Having pledged support for the project, but also promised to scrutinise — Labor has a fine line to walk.
It also needs to contend with its troubled history on the project, which it previously didn't support.
The opposition is clearly being careful not to be seen as wavering in its support for the stadium.
But the party's managed to ask plenty of tough questions about the bungled Spirit of Tasmania project without appearing not to support it.
The 23,000-seat roofed stadium was a condition from the AFL for the Tasmania Devils to enter the competition. ( Supplied: Tasmania Football Club )
While debate may be fierce in the parliament, many in the public won't care that this commitment's been broken.
They may see the project as still worth the cost. Perhaps for them, there was no such thing as a price too high.
It's about an AFL Team — something that holds an unparalleled place in the collective Tasmanian psyche.
In the parliament yesterday, Independent MP David O'Byrne spoke of the power of the Devils.

"I have seen in working-class suburbs that are at ground zero of disadvantage … having the [Tasmania] Devils and the hope of an AFL team, getting those kids to turn up to school in Devils' gear," he told the chamber.
"Because in one of the schools in my electorate there are two Devils players who work at that school.
It's those arguments the government can use to sway the final few Tasmanians yet to form a decision on the project.
Benefits that may become more apparent as construction begins, and the Devils run out for their first AFL match.

items.title: How Victoria's election landscape could shape One Nation's fortunes
paras: One Nation Victoria leader Warren Pickering is contesting the lower house seat of Pakenham in Melbourne's south-east. ( AAP: Jay Kogler )
One Nation had its best ever statewide result at an election in March this year, when 22.9 per cent of South Australians voted for the party founded by Pauline Hanson.

It's trying to improve on that result this week, and the party's rise is the main reason that whoever wins the looming Victorian election will likely win it with a record low primary vote in the state.
With the party now trailing the Coalition in opinion polls by quite some margin, the number of seats in which it can expect to lead its conservative rival has narrowed as election day approaches.
The party is still expected to have a statewide vote above 20 per cent, meaning we'll see some very big primary votes in some seats.
The risk for the party is that it sees a repeat of what happened in South Australia in March, where One Nation came second in a long list of seats around the state.
Federal One Nation leader Pauline Hanson attended the party's Victorian campaign launch in Melbourne last month. ( ABC News )

In general, One Nation has a much better chance of winning seats when the Coalition is weak. That was clearly the case in South Australia, but Jess Wilson's Coalition is in a much stronger position than the SA Liberals.

Barnaby Joyce acknowledged on the ABC's Afternoon Briefing just before early voting began that "it will be tough" to win many seats, seeking to downplay the importance of the Victorian election by calling it a "peculiar circumstance".
"We've had … the most atrocious government in the 60,000 years of human habitation on the Australian continent … the Labor Party will come third," he said.
The pattern of One Nation support across the country hasn't really changed through its peaks and troughs over the years.
The party polls highest in rural and regional seats, and in the cities its strongest vote has been in the outer suburbs. The party has always performed very poorly in inner-city seats.

We can see this picture by mapping the results of the 2025 election onto Victoria's electorates. This map shows the state districts with the One Nation result in the Senate election at all polling booths in that district.
One Nation is now polling much more strongly statewide than it did in mid-2025, so these figures are not a prediction of the result in the upcoming election.
But the map suggests we should be watching seats along Victoria's northern border, as well as eastern Victorian seats like Gippsland East and Narracan for One Nation's strongest primary votes.

Morwell saw One Nation's strongest Senate result last year, and may be one of the party's best prospects of winning a seat. It has been held by Labor, Liberal, and Nationals members in its history and also elected an independent in 2018.

In Melbourne, it's outer-suburban seats like Melton and Sunbury in the west, and Pakenham in the south-east — where leader Warren Pickering is running — that we'd expect to see some of the highest One Nation numbers.

That pattern of support aligns with research into the demographics of Pauline Hanson supporters. Research in August conducted by former Labor pollster John Utting and former Labor adviser Bruce Hawker concluded that One Nation's support had become "considerably more entrenched", and that "tradies are the heartland of One Nation support".
Indeed, in South Australia's state election this year, there was a relationship between One Nation's vote and the number of people who had a vocational certificate or no post-school education.
In the seats with the highest concentration of them, the party got around a third of the vote.
In last year's federal election we also saw a correlation between One Nation's vote and the number of adults who don't have a university degree or diploma.

This could help explain why the party may attract strong support in the multicultural parts of Melbourne despite its focus on migration. The research suggests that ancestry or nationality are weaker predictors of the party's vote.
Peculiarly, the districts where One Nation achieves some of its highest first preference votes may not end up being the seats it has the best chances of winning.
That's because preferences in regional Victoria, where we expect many races to be a contest between the Nationals and One Nation, are unlikely to favour the insurgent party.
Labor, Greens, and independent preferences are unlikely to help One Nation, meaning the party would need to have enough of a primary vote lead to withstand the flow of preferences against it.

For example, in the South Australian electorate of Narungga in March, One Nation needed a first preference lead of 15 percentage points to win the seat. After preferences, the party won by just 58 votes.

In Melbourne, however, Liberal preferences are likely to help One Nation over Labor, meaning the party can win with less of a buffer. MRP models conducted earlier in the year, when One Nations prospects looked stronger, suggested nearly all of the party's gains would come from Labor rather than the Coalition.
Now, the party's challenge might be beating the Liberal Party's primary vote in order to be in a position to benefit from those flows.

In South Australia's election in March, it was able to do this across all of Adelaide's outer suburbs, but that was against a particularly weak Liberal Party that saw its support crash to the single digits in many seats. Against a more credible Liberal Party in Melbourne, will it be able to come out on top in the city's outer suburbs?
One thing working in One Nation's favour is that in the western and northern suburbs there is a vein of discontent it may be able to tap.

In the 2022 election, Labor's primary vote fell most dramatically in these parts of the city, many of which were areas that would have felt the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic more acutely, with lower levels of wealth and less ability to work from home.

These were some of the government's safest seats, but they saw some of the largest swings of the election, revealing a real vulnerability for Labor in some of the districts it has been able to rely on for decades.
However, in most of the seats with the biggest drops in Labor primary vote, the Coalition wasn't the beneficiary.

Labor's vote was down by 18 to 20 percentage points in Kororoit, Greenvale, St Albans, and Sydenham, but the Liberal primary barely grew while a variety of right-wing minor parties grew their vote by up to 15 percentage points.
In Melton, a crowded field of minor parties and independents received 38 per cent of the vote.

Seats where minor parties polled strongly could present an opportunity for One Nation. If the party can consolidate that 2022 protest vote, it has a strong starting point to build on in its fight to overtake the Liberal Party.
But the Liberals still cannot be counted out in these seats and, like many contests across the state, it may come down to who can poll strongly enough to reach second place.

The multi-party contest playing out in Victoria brings with it a lot of uncertainty, and relatively small changes in the statewide vote could bring large changes in the shape of the contest and the seat hauls for each of the parties.
On election night, we need to pay far closer attention to who is coming third in each seat than usual.

items.title: ASIC following up on more allegations of misconduct by consulting giants
paras: Advertisement Business Companies Consulting ASIC following up on more allegations of misconduct by consulting giants Colin Kruger November 25, 2026 — 5:05am
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Share A A A The corporate regulator is investigating 35 allegations of serious misconduct following a probe of Australia’s audit giants, and is referring other complaints to professional bodies for further investigation.

The action comes after the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) uncovered 558 audit-related complaints earlier this year , having used its compulsory information gathering powers to access internal complaints at consultants KPMG, EY, Deloitte and PwC staff in the three years from July 2023.

ASIC has stepped up its surveillance of the Big Four audit firms after KPMG’s whistleblower scandal. Paul Rovere “ASIC has identified 35 complaints involving potential statutory audit conduct issues or misuse of audit client information from a review of internal complaints at Australia’s four largest audit firms,” the regulator said.
“Some complaints contained serious allegations of misconduct that ASIC is examining through enforcement and targeted industry surveillance work.”
The surveillance was conducted by ASIC in response to the KPMG scandal this year, where a whistleblower alleged senior partners misused confidential client information to win new audit business.

Some of the allegations have now been substantiated, senior KPMG executives have been forced to resign and hundreds of jobs have been slashed as lucrative clients like Macquarie Group walked away from the firm.
ASIC did not say whether the latest complaints related to all four audit firms dominating Australia’s corporate landscape and boardrooms.

ASIC’s report said there have also been other issues identified which relate to matters it is already investigating, including “several matters which have been referred for consideration as part of our existing investigations into KPMG about misstatements in transparency reporting”.
This relates to KPMG allegedly failing to report internal whistleblower complaints.

ASIC highlighted the seriousness of the latest allegations, given these four firms audit more than 94 per cent of Australia’s listed companies by market valuation, and 85 per cent of registrable superannuation entities.

“Auditors are gatekeepers to Australia’s financial markets. Investors, businesses and superannuation members rely on them to scrutinise financial information with independence, integrity and professional scepticism,” ASIC Commissioner Kate O’Rourke said.

ASIC Commissioner Kate O’Rourke during a Senate estimates hearing at Parliament House in Canberra. Alex Ellinghausen O’Rourke said some of the issues identified from the internal complaints include directions to not escalate audit concerns, failure to escalate material audit issues, breaches of confidentiality and victimisation of employees who reported issues.

“Internal complaints can provide valuable intelligence regarding deficiencies with how statutory audits are conducted. Audit firms should carefully and thoroughly interrogate complaints to identify and address these issues,” O’Rourke said.

ASIC noted there are no regulatory provisions directly governing how audit firms handle internal complaints and said it did not investigate every complaint in detail, or reach findings about every person mentioned in the complaints.

Most of the 558 complaints fell outside ASIC’s regulatory powers. It said some of the allegations, which include bullying and sexual harassment, have been referred to other regulators – including Chartered Accountants ANZ, CPA Australia and the Tax Practitioners Board for possible breaches of professional and ethical standards.
ASIC said it has already released information in relation to a number of individuals, and is continuing to engage with these other regulators around additional matters of potential interest.
The corporate watchdog said its work is ongoing, and it will continue to communicate the outcomes of any further regulatory action.

Just last week, KPMG said it is cutting 230 jobs as the fallout from the whistleblower scandal continues. The job cuts are mostly in its consulting division, with smaller cuts in supporting areas and the team that advises companies on corporate deals.
“We must align our business with client demand. This is a necessary step towards renewing and rebuilding our firm,” KPMG’s recently appointed chief executive John Sams said.
State and federal governments have banned KPMG from winning new work since the full scale of the whistleblower scandal became clear.

items.title: RBI issues Draft Amendment Directions for ‘Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)’
paras: The Reserve Bank had issued the Amendment Directions dated June 24, 2026 on ‘ Customer Protection in Fraudulent Electronic Banking Transactions ’ which, inter alia, strengthened the existing framework for limiting liability of customers in unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs). While the revised framework primarily addresses customer liability in the event of fraudulent EBTs, a need is felt to strengthen the same from a preventive perspective by providing customers with greater control over the manner and extent to which digital payment channels may be used. Further, on a review to bring in uniformity in practices adopted by banks and ensure that customers are protected against specific acts of omission or commission on part of the banks, it has been decided to expand the scope of the definition of ‘negligence by a bank’ specified in the aforementioned Amendment Directions. 2. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank has today issued the following draft Amendment Directions for public comments, which propose to amend Directions on Responsible Business Conduct issued by the Department of Regulation, RBI: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Payments Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Rural Co-operative Banks - Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 3. The comments / feedback on the draft Amendment Directions may be submitted by the regulated entities and members of public / other stakeholders on or before December 14, 2026 through the following channels: the ‘ Connect 2 Regulate ’ section on the website by following the corresponding hyperlink provided against each document in the page where they are hosted; or by email with the subject line ‘Feedback on (full name of the draft Amendment Directions (including the type of Regulated Entity))’. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1548

items.title: RBI releases 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs)
paras: State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank continue to be identified as Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) under the same bucketing structure as in the 2025 list of D-SIBs . The additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) requirement for these D-SIBs will be in addition to the capital conservation buffer. The list of D-SIBs is as follows: Bucket Banks Additional Common Equity Tier 1 requirement as a percentage of Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs) 5 - 1% 4 State Bank of India 0.80% 3 - 0.60% 2 HDFC Bank 0.40% 1 ICICI Bank 0.20% Background: The Reserve Bank had issued the Framework for dealing with Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) on July 22, 2014 , which was subsequently updated on December 28, 2023 . The D-SIB framework requires the Reserve Bank to disclose the names of banks designated as D-SIBs starting from 2015 and place these banks in appropriate buckets depending upon their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs). Based on the bucket in which a D-SIB is placed, an additional common equity requirement has to be applied to it. In case a foreign bank having branch presence in India is a Global Systemically Important Bank (G-SIB) , it has to maintain additional CET1 capital surcharge in India as applicable to it as a G-SIB, proportionate to its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs) in India, i.e., additional CET1 buffer prescribed by the home regulator (amount) multiplied by India RWA as per consolidated global Group books divided by total consolidated global Group RWA. The Reserve Bank had announced SBI and ICICI Bank as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016 while HDFC Bank was classified as D-SIB in 2017 along with SBI and ICICI Bank. The current update is based on the data collected from banks as on March 31, 2026. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1547

items.title: Governor, Reserve Bank of India meets Managing Directors & Chief Executive Officers of select NBFCs, HFCs and Industry R
paras: As part of the Reserve Bank’s ongoing engagement with regulated entities, the Governor, Reserve Bank of India, today met in Mumbai with the Managing Directors and Chief Executive Officers (MDs & CEOs) of select Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), including Government NBFCs, Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) and Microfinance Institutions. Representatives of Sa-Dhan, the Micro Finance Institutions Network (MFIN) and the Finance Industry Development Council (FIDC) also participated. Deputy Governors Shri Swaminathan J., Dr Poonam Gupta, Shri S. C. Murmu and Shri Rohit Jain attended the meeting, along with other senior officers of the Reserve Bank. The MD & CEO of the National Housing Bank also participated. The Governor acknowledged the role of NBFCs and HFCs in supporting economic activity by widening access to credit. He emphasised the need for responsible and sustainable credit growth and urged NBFCs to put customers first as they expand their business. He highlighted the importance of quality service, effective grievance redressal and fair recovery practices. He also encouraged NBFCs to use the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR) for customer onboarding and to keep customer records in the registry up to date to improve customer convenience. The Governor urged participants to strengthen their cybersecurity infrastructure and adopt a comprehensive, risk-based approach to managing cyber and IT risks, with appropriate oversight by their boards and senior management. Participants shared feedback on policy and operational matters concerning the NBFC sector. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1554

items.title: Reserve Bank (Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026
paras: The Reserve Bank of India had, on July 27, 2026 , issued the Draft (Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions for stakeholder feedback. 2. Feedback received on the draft Directions has been examined and consequent modifications, as deemed appropriate, have been suitably incorporated in the final Directions. A statement on the feedback received on the draft Directions is provided in the Annex . 3. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank has today issued the final Amendment Directions as given below: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks – Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 Reserve Bank of India (All India Financial Institutions – Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026 5. The guidelines will come into force from April 01, 2027. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-2027/1550

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "India matters most for future of planet" says British High Commissioner Lindy Cameron
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): In recent times when climate change has become a pressing issue with countries across the world being ravaged due to climate catastrophes, it becomes imperative to discuss and deliberate upon global actions that can help the world rise up and meet these challenges. At the NDTV World Summit's a discussion was held on the theme, "India Matters The Most For Future Of Planet". Participants in the discussion included Erik Solheim, Former Minister of Climate and the Environment of Norway; Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India; Shishir Priyadarshi, President Chintan Research Foundation; Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative. "India is the country that matters the most for the future of the planet and climate change. India's ambition for development should not in any way be constrained by the responsibilities of the planet," Lindy Cameron , British High Commissioner to India, emphasised. She noted that the UK is committed towards the Multilateral Development Banks (MDB) reforms, technology and research support in India to aid the efforts. "Every dollar invested in resilient infrastructure pays 4 times over," said Cameron. "Lived experience of climate emergencies helps people to understand why their government needs to take policy action now," she added. Further talking about the need for urgent government action, Harjeet Singh, Global Engagement Director, Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said, "Series of disasters affecting both developed and developing countries are serving as a wake-up call. As rich countries will get more and more affected by climate change which they did not imagine till a couple of years ago, most vulnerable countries are going to be struggling with impacts who also have very less capacity to deal with it. India is taking a leadership role in the global fight against climate change. Initiatives such as Global Biofuels Alliance, International Solar Alliance, and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure are some efforts taken by India in recent years to manage the climate crisis. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
paras: smoke gets in your beer How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops Study: Brewers can still use up to 50% of smoke-tainted hops without affecting beer taste and aroma.

2 ... ... ... Credit: Ellie Lafferty Credit: Ellie Lafferty Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this “smoke taint” adversely affected not only local wine production , but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant.

That’s why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on how much tainted hops are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists.

As previously reported , the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, i n 2018 , OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper— identified the growing popularity of “ dry hopping ” (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon.

All beer contains hops, a key flavoring agent that also imparts useful antimicrobial properties. (Beer spoils quickly without them.) Brewers mash and steep grain in hot water, which converts all that starch into sugars. This is traditionally the stage where hops are added to the liquid extract (wort) and boiled to give the beer that hint of bitterness. During the boiling process, a portion of the resins (alpha acids) in hops isomerize into iso-alpha acids. That chemical rearrangement of the molecules is what produces bitterness. Yeast is then added to trigger fermentation, turning the sugars into alcohol.

Far from being the chemically inert ingredient brewers have long assumed, hops contain starch enzymes that, under certain conditions, can boost their activity to such a great extent that excessive re-fermentation occurs (“hop-creep”) after bottling. Dry-hopped beers produce significantly higher CO2 levels and packaging pressures, because there is much more re-fermentation going on than usual. And sometimes that pressure builds until the bottle explodes.

In the wake of the 2020 wildfires, Shellhammer turned his attention to smoke-tainted hops. The primary culprit is volatile phenols (VP), which are produced when the lignin in plant cells is exposed to the high heat of a wildfire. Earlier this year, the OSU team discovered that smoke exposure while the hops are drying increased VP uptake and substantially altered the hops’ aroma; those with higher levels took on meaty, smoky, and artificial BBQ notes; medicinal flavors have also been reported. Those notes were so strong that they overpowered more desirable beery qualities, like citrus notes or aroma intensity.

For this latest project, Shellhammer worked with graduate student Cade Jobe to harvest Idaho-grown Cascade hops. Then they “smoked” the hops in kilns using wood pellets injected into the air intake systems, then dried them. They also harvested and dried non-smoked hops as a control.
Credit: Ellie Lafferty/Oregon State University Credit: Ellie Lafferty/Oregon State University

Next, Shellhammer and Jobe brewed several batches of beer, blending smoke-tainted hops with untainted hops at different levels (25, 50, and 75 percent), along with beer brewed using only tainted hops and beer brewed with no tainted hops. They did this using both a dry-hopping process and one where they added hops during wort boiling. They measured the VP concentrations of each batch of beer with gas chromatography. Finally, a panel of 24 blind tasters evaluated each beer.

Shellhammer and Jobe found that dry-hopping with smoke-tainted hops resulted in increased VP concentrations; the more tainted hops were included, the higher those concentrations. The tasters reported more intense smoky aromas in those beers as well as meaty, smoky, medicinal, and artificial BBQ flavors.

By contrast, when tainted hops were added during the boil, the resulting beer was pretty much indistinguishable from beers brewed with no smoke-tainted hops, even though the former still showed the same increases in VP concentrations. There was no discernible difference when hops were added during the wort boiling stage.

The authors suggest brewers could blend smoke-tainted hops with untainted batches when dry-hopping, keeping the smoke-tainted hops to less than 50 percent. This would still allow brewers to use tainted batches of hops, reducing the economic impact of wildfires on beer production.

“Hop growers and brewers are looking for guidance on whether and how to use smoke-affected hops,” said Jobe . “This research begins to provide some practical information to help hop growers and brewers understand how smoky hops impact beer so that they can make the best decisions.”

There’s still more research to be done to confirm the precise ratios and to replicate these initial findings. Future research should also explore the impact of hops exposed to smoke under field conditions, when the plant is still metabolically active, along with consumer studies to evaluate whether beer drinkers more generally will find the flavors of beers made with blended hops (tainted and untainted) acceptable. The findings may not extend to wine production, however, since the fermentation processes are so different, per the authors. And grapes comprise almost all the raw materials in wine, while hops are a smaller fraction of beer brewing ingredients.
Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists, 2026. DOI: 10.1080/03610470.2026.2749166 ( About DOIs ).

items.title: Kalshi makes “difficult decision” to halt Utah trading after losing court fights
paras: “One GOP move I can get behind” Kalshi makes “difficult decision” to halt Utah trading after losing court fights Kalshi’s pause in Utah draws cheers as critics bash ads and boo insider trading.

10 ... ... ... Credit: Mitch Diamond | Photodisc Credit: Mitch Diamond | Photodisc Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick said Monday.

It seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there. In Utah, several lawsuits are still playing out, and Kalshi also lost a bid to persuade a federal appeals court to block those cases until the appeal is resolved.

Kalshi also wasn’t saved by an emergency motion from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission—which argues that the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction market trading. At this time, the federal district court has not granted that motion to block Utah’s enforcement actions, either.

“This is an unfortunate outcome for the more than 177,000 Utahns who use Kalshi,” McGavick said. “We will continue to fight this in court, and we look forward to returning to Utah once our legal position is vindicated.”
Utah’s attorney general, Derek Brown, had filed both civil and criminal charges against Kalshi , as he defended the state’s 130-year ban on gambling.

In a press release discussing the initial lawsuit, he accused Kalshi of running “an online casino” that violates the state’s constitution. “Not only do our state laws ban gambling but Utah is one of only two states where gambling is also prohibited under the state constitution,” Brown said. “For 130 years, Utah has been clear: gambling has no place here, and we will enforce our laws.”

Late Monday, a major Utah area news outlet, KSL.com, reported that Brown was prepared to jail Kalshi’s co-founders, who had been summoned to be booked on 14 charges on December 5. He defended those plans, saying, “There is a question I have seen from people asking, ‘Well, do we modify this booking process if someone is a very wealthy and well-known tech billionaire?’ and the answer is ‘No, the process is the process; we don’t modify it based on who you are.”

However, on Tuesday, Utah decided to drop the criminal charges against Kalshi, McGavick confirmed to Ars. In a statement on X, Kalshi general counsel, Yaakov Roth, said that “we are pleased that Utah has chosen to dismiss criminal charges against Kalshi, while proceeding with civil litigation. Good faith jurisdictional disagreements should never be criminalized. We stand ready to work with State AGs on reasonable interim measures until courts resolve the dispute over who regulates prediction markets.”
In a press release , Brown explained that the charges were dropped specifically due to the pause.

“Kalshi said it would geofence Utah, which blocks access to its site in the state,” the press release said. “The company also committed to monitor for Utah-based IP addresses trying to reach its site. The Office then reevaluated its position and moved to dismiss the criminal case against the company and the individual defendants.”
Brown threatened that the charges would be raised again if Kalshi tried to renew operations.

“Utah does not allow gambling, and prediction markets are gambling,” Brown said. Kalshi has pulled out of Utah, and if it returns, so will the charges. Every company in this space should take note. If they promote, support, or enable gambling, we will hold them accountable.”
Discussion of the Kalshi pause in a Utah sub-Reddit found some Redditors skeptical of the state’s cases as potentially overreaching.

However, many top commenters seemed pleased with the enforcement efforts, suggesting that Utah may have bipartisan support among some residents. One commenter cheered on the attorney general’s efforts as “the one item in the Utah GOP’s agenda I can get behind,” while another agreed that “prediction markets are incredibly toxic and are manipulated against ordinary people.”

Many complained about Kalshi ads flooding their social media feeds. Some suggested the state should focus on banning advertising of prediction markets, while potentially still allowing adults to trade on event contracts if they want to throw their “money away.”
Fears of insider trading were also raised. One comment laid out why prediction markets seem suspiciously designed to promote insider trading and other market manipulation:

“I’m pretty libertarian and hate banning things. But gambling and prediction markets are a scourge. Even the term ‘prediction market’ is a misnomer. Because ultimately when people with big dollars get involved it creates a financial incentive for them to make fucked up things happen in the real world. Think about it, decades ago we understood that sports betting was a problem because it corrupted sports—s omething that ultimately is pretty meaningless. Then we got all these people betting on the stock market with puts and it created huge incentives to cause havoc with markets. Now if people are betting big money on politics and wars and everything else, it just means people with influence can make money by making improbable/unexpected things happen.”
One commenter joked, “I wonder how Kashi would have reacted if the judge in charge of their case had ‘traded’ $500,000 on the event of them losing the case. Not a problem at all, right?”

On the same day Kalshi announced its temporary pause in Utah, a judge rejected a request from New York’s attorney general, Letitia James, to immediately shut down Kalshi in that state, Courthouse News reported .

New York Supreme Court Justice Melissa Crane said she was “uncomfortable” granting the temporary restraining order so early in the case because “there does seem to be an indication that there would be market disruption that I’m concerned about.” Kalshi attorney Grant Mainland described it a little differently, claiming that a sudden halt would cause a “market emergency.”

“I think this is the ultimate relief in the case, which is improper for me to do without full briefing,” Crane said. Instead of granting James’ request, she recommended that Kalshi take steps to address the state’s top concerns by considering “safeguards for users between 18 and 20,” who are under the state’s legal gambling age, Courthouse News reported.

According to Kalshi’s estimates, New York’s Kalshi user base (1.5 million) is much larger than Utah’s, so the market disruption from the Utah shutdown may not have carried the same dire stakes for Kalshi or its broader user base.

The CFTC has sought to intervene in that case, too, and it seems clear that Kalshi expects the questions of who can regulate prediction markets and what trading qualifies as a “bet” to reach the Supreme Court. Kalshi’s spokesperson did not respond to Ars’ questions on how the Utah pause broadly impacted users or the platform.

So far, “three federal appeals courts have ruled that states can regulate prediction markets, while a fourth found they cannot,” Courthouse News reported. But despite the current balance tipping toward allowing states to regulate prediction markets, Kalshi appears confident that the Supreme Court will resolve the disparate court rulings in its favor.

In a lawsuit filed by a disgruntled Kalshi user, Kalshi argued that it would waste lower courts’ time to continue litigating these cases and that no case should be resolved until the Supreme Court weighs in.
In that case, Kalshi user Scott Bright alleged that he lost more than $300,000 on sports bets that were technically illegal in Washington.

According to Kalshi, all of Bright’s claims rest “on the premise that state gambling laws reach KalshiEX’s federally regulated exchange—the question now before the Supreme Court. Plaintiff puts the cart before the horse; Defendants ask only that the Court let that threshold question be resolved first.”

The court has yet to address Kalshi’s request to stay the case, but Bright has argued that Kalshi is trying to “sideline a case governed by binding Ninth Circuit precedent so that they can wait for a Supreme Court decision that may never come.”

Kalshi did not respond to Ars’ request for a statement on Bright’s lawsuit. In their court filing, they argued that “a stay will let the Supreme Court address an issue that could dispose of every claim, will not meaningfully harm Plaintiff, and will spare Defendants and the Court litigation under a framework that may soon be displaced.”

items.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
paras: No robots! Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted AI songs account for 6.3 percent of Tidal’s catalog, but it’s about to be zero.

21 ... ... ... Credit: Thomas Trutschel/Photothek via Getty Images Credit: Thomas Trutschel/Photothek via Getty Images Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists.

Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn’t enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated.

As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal’s total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it’s only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements.

Some people don’t particularly mind AI music, but the team at Tidal has come to believe the harm to artists is too great. AI models can pump out random noises faster than humans can create things of real value, which can mislead listeners and siphon royalty payments away from creators. There’s also an issue with AI uploaders actively attempting to steal royalty payments. Tidal says it has already removed about 66,000 tracks from its service for impersonating artists, which was against its AI policy even before this update.
As of December 9, individual uploaders and distributors will no longer be allowed to add AI music to Tidal. However, they could lie, couldn’t they?

Tidal hasn’t specified how it detects AI music, but it will probably rely on watermarking. Almost every AI song on Tidal (94 percent) comes from Suno, which added watermarking earlier this year. Tidal also cites Google Lyria as a source of AI tunes, which has SynthID labels embedded in the waveform. Deezer claimed it has a licensable AI music detector with a false-positive rate of less than 0.01 percent, but it’s unclear if Tidal is using that or something similar.

That will take care of most AI music, but this approach won’t detect everything. There are open models for music generation that you can run locally on a GPU, and some cloud-based providers aren’t bothering to watermark their outputs. Even if Tidal is using a separate detection system, new models may be able to evade it—it’s always going to be a cat-and-mouse game. This will be a problem with verifying provenance in all types of media in the future. For the time being, at least, Tidal’s policy should clear out most of the AI slop.

The people directing robots to make these songs will have plenty of other options after Tidal blocks AI. Spotify, YouTube Music , Deezer, and Apple Music all allow AI music on their platforms with labeling. Spotify has removed millions of AI tracks from its collection based on user feedback. Other streamers haven’t specified how much slop (if any) they’ve cleared out.

items.title: Jannik Sinner releases statement after successful knee surgery, ‘See you soon’
paras: Jannik Sinner underwent knee surgery on Tuesday morning ahead of his return to tennis next year. After weeks of speculation, Sinner and his team decided surgery was necessary .

He travelled to Turku, Finland, for the surgery with specialist Lasse Lempainen, and the early signs seem positive. Sinner, who hasn’t played a match since July, has now posted on social media confirming the success of the surgery.

The Italian explained why he waited until November for the surgery, having already been out injured for several months. “Over the past few months, together with my team, we’ve tried everything to treat my injury without surgery. After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn’t respond as we’d all hoped,” said Sinner on Instagram . “That’s why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band.
items.impact: Sinner is expected to miss the Six Kings Slam and the Australian Open while recovering from knee surgery.

items.title: Carlos Alcaraz can match one of Novak Djokovic’s personal records at the 2027 Australian Open
paras: The Spaniard compiled a 25-2 record upon returning from long-term injury at the end of August, winning the Japan Open, Vienna Open, Paris Masters and the ATP Finals .
After capturing the title in Turin, Italy , Alcaraz has only four significant titles missing from his trophy room: the Canadian Open, Shanghai Masters, Davis Cup and an Olympic gold medal.

As has been the case over the past few years, Alcaraz will enter every Grand Slam event in 2027 as one of the favourites. The 23-year-old will almost certainly have extra motivation to capture as many major titles as possible next year, as he has the opportunity to equal one of Novak Djokovic’s personal achievements. Carlos Alcaraz’s victory over Novak Djokovic in the 2026 Australian Open final ensured that the Spaniard would go five consecutive years with at least one Grand Slam triumph.

items.title: Andy Roddick slams Alexander Zverev’s critics after ATP Finals loss, ‘This is so stupid’
paras: Alexander Zverev lost to Carlos Alcaraz, 2-6, 6-7, in the 2026 ATP Finals final. Despite winning two Grand Slam titles and reaching world number one, many still doubt Zverev .

Some critics point to his record against top-10 players this year (7-10) and to the fact that he didn’t beat either of his two biggest rivals, Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner, in 2026 (0-7). Former world number one and 2003 US Open champion Andy Roddick has now delivered his verdict on Zverev’s 2026 season, hitting back at some of the German’s harshest critics.

Do I believe that when he’s fully healthy, he is better than Carlos [Alcaraz] and Jannik [Sinner]? Who cares?” he said during the latest episode of ‘ Served with Andy Roddick ‘. “For all the people who are criticising and mad, he is number one in the world.
items.impact: Michael Stich was Germany’s star man when they beat Australia 4-1 in Dusseldorf, 33 years ago.
